summary.headline: BMW Industries posted record FY26 PAT of INR81 crores (11.9% margin) and Q4 PAT of INR33 crores; Bokaro phase one commissioning is set to start in Q1 FY27.
summary.overview: Management reported record quarterly and annual profits, with Q4 operating income of INR210 crores, operating EBITDA of INR58 crores (27.5% margin) and PAT of INR33 crores (15.4% margin). For FY26, operating income was INR665 crores, EBITDA INR165 crores (24.8%) and PAT INR81 crores (11.9%). CRM complex output rose to about 718,000 MT with utilisation at 70.9% annualised, and pipes and tubes output rose to 201,000 MT from about 177,000 MT. The focus has shifted to the Bokaro greenfield downstream steel complex, with cold trials guided before end-May 2026 and hot trials in June; meaningful Bokaro sales are expected from Q2 FY27.

financial_highlights.value: INR364 crores; net debt to equity 0.45x (0.27x excluding Bokaro borrowings)
About INR150 crores at FY26 vs about INR80 crores at FY25
financial_highlights.change: Attributed to one key customer delaying payment; received early April

segments.name: CRM complex (downstream steel)
segments.commentary: Production rose to about 718,000 MT in FY26; annualised utilisation 70.9% vs 66.9% in December quarter.

segments.name: Pipes and tubes
segments.commentary: Production rose to 201,000 MT in FY26 from about 177,000 MT in FY25; installed capacity increased from under 6 lakh tons to about 7.32 lakh tons, with utilisation about 34.2%.

segments.name: Bokaro greenfield complex
segments.commentary: Total cost about INR803 crores; phased commissioning from Q1 FY27 starting with colour coating, followed by Galvalume, cold rolling and pickling. Peak capacity about 6 lakh tons of saleable product.

guidance_outlook: Reiterated about 75% revenue CAGR over FY25 to FY28 (three-year compounded, not annual), with operating EBITDA CAGR of about 45% and PAT CAGR of about 40% over the same period.
Blended EBITDA margin expected to stabilise at about 12% to 13% and PAT margin at about 5% to 6% by FY28 (corrected from 13-14% on the call).
Existing-business tubes utilisation expected to rise from about 33-34% to 60-65% over the next 2 to 3 years; no meaningful investment planned in the existing business.
Existing business revenue at peak utilisation estimated at INR800-900 crores (management agreed with analyst's framing).
Bokaro target working capital cycle of about 30 days, or 30-40 days comfortable; blended ROCE expected at 15%+.
Bokaro long-term debt expected to peak in the next 12 to 15 months; analyst's FY28 total debt of INR700-800 crores accepted as fair.
Subsidies under Jharkhand policy, PLI or similar to be used for debt repayment; not included in projections.
capex_capacity: Bokaro greenfield downstream steel complex: phased commissioning from Q1 FY27; colour coating first, then Galvalume, cold rolling and pickling; cold trials before end-May 2026 and hot trials in June 2026.

Bokaro capacity mix: about 5-6 lakh tons galvanising/GI/ZAM, 3-4 lakh tons cold rolling, 5-6 lakh tons pickling (quoted as 500,000-600,000 tons), about 2 lakh tons colour coating; leftover 3-4 lakh tons as galvanised, Galvalume or ZAM, with peak sales about 6 lakh tons.

Total project cost about INR803 crores; INR109 crores of internal accruals invested to date and INR143 crores of debt drawn for Bokaro; funding roughly 250-300 equity to remaining debt, primarily from current cash flows.
Partnership with Indian Oil Corporation for piped natural gas supply at Bokaro.
Pipes and tubes installed capacity increased to about 7.32 lakh tons.
demand_pricing: Management declined to give revenue ranges for Bokaro phase one or quarter-wise guidance; the first-quarter contribution will not be clubbed with Q2 numbers.
Order book not yet built as plants are not commissioned; order-to-delivery gap about two weeks; long forward orders are avoided due to zinc, aluminium and magnesium price volatility.
Spreads described as fairly stable over long-term averages with short-term aberrations; long-term spreads positive.
ZAM (zinc-aluminium-magnesium) claimed to give 5-6x the life of zinc at the same coating; a marginal premium over GI is expected, with no quantification.
Zinc price cited at about INR3-3.25 lakh per ton.
Bokaro sales to be under the BMW brand, B2B focus; marketing already started with potential buyers; no conversion partners in talks at Bokaro. Export markets to be pursued but no share quantified.
Existing business revenue is conversion-only (no raw material in cost of sales); Bokaro will add raw material cost and inflate absolute sales.

qa_highlights.question: Breakup of consolidated EBITDA margin and Bokaro contribution over the next 2-3 years; can revenue reach INR800-900 crores from existing business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management corrected the target to 12-13% EBITDA margin, confirmed INR800-900 crores as a fair peak for the existing business, and linked uplift to tubes utilisation rising to 60-65%.

qa_highlights.question: Expected IRR on the INR800-odd crore Bokaro project?
qa_highlights.answer: Base-case investment hurdle is 20% IRR, and management said the project is expected to be above that.

qa_highlights.question: Phase-one ramp-up and dilution of EBITDA, plus depreciation and interest accounting from Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: No quarterly or FY27 revenue guidance; dilution should be seen as a change in business model (conversion to buy-and-sell); assets capitalised phase-wise as commissioned.

qa_highlights.question: Jharkhand incentives quantification and Bokaro technology/EPC partner?
qa_highlights.answer: Incentives not quantified or included in projections; any subsidies to repay debt. Technology is not new; equipment vendors used, not L&T, with locally available partners.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital cycle and peak debt post-Bokaro?
qa_highlights.answer: Target working capital cycle about 30 days (30-40 days comfortable); long-term debt peaks in 12-15 months; analyst's total debt of INR700-800 crores by FY28 accepted.

qa_highlights.question: Blended ROCE and funding mix for the INR803 crore project?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended ROCE expected at 15%+; funding roughly 250-300 equity-to-debt ratio as stated, primarily from internal cash flows.

risks_watch: Bokaro commissioning timing: cold trials guided before end-May and hot trials in June; any slippage would delay saleable output and the Q2 sales ramp.
Ramp-up risk: management acknowledged quality, volume and product acceptance stabilisation will take time after production starts.
Margin transition: the shift to buy-and-sell model adds raw material cost and may dilute percentage margins, and management has not quantified the FY27 impact.
Receivables: about INR150 crores at FY26 (vs INR80 crores) due to one key customer's delayed payment; monitor collection in Q1 FY27.
Commodity volatility in zinc, aluminium and magnesium; company avoids long forward orders without hedging.
Existing pipes and tubes utilisation about 34%; reaching 60-65% is a multi-year target. TMT rolling mill faces customer-side raw material constraints.
Subsidy income under Jharkhand policy is not in projections and will go to debt repayment.
Peak debt expected in 12-15 months; monitor debt levels against the INR700-800 crore FY28 range discussed.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the growth roadmap and FY26 results, but deliberately vague on Bokaro phase-one revenue, quarterly numbers, order book and product-level margins, deferring these to later calls. Management also corrected its own EBITDA margin figure on the call and declined to compare directly with listed peer Manaksia on product mix.
key_quotes: We are delighted to report our highest ever quarterly and annual profits.

We reiterate our earlier guidance of a CAGR of approximately 75% over FY '25 to FY '28 period supported by the phased commissioning and ramp -up of Bokaro greenfield project along with continued organic growth across the existing business verticals.
So it's not really a dilution if you consider the change in model.
So on a blended basis, we expect to reach 15 plus.

growth.why: Management reiterated ~75% three-year compounded revenue CAGR over FY25-FY28 (EBITDA ~45%, PAT ~40%), backed by Bokaro's ~INR803 crore greenfield complex entering phased commissioning (cold trials before end-May 2026, hot trials June, sales from Q2 FY27) and tubes utilisation rising from ~34% to 60-65%, but no order book exists yet and management declined to quantify Bokaro phase-one revenue.
